outcome.technical: DRIVER (drive-phase.py). Rule A: the step owns the scratch checkout - own_checkouts(ctx, run) wraps drive_locked in drive() and holds {commit: (tree, holder)} under ctx[SCRATCH_KEY]; step_checkout(ctx, commit) makes it at the first ask that needs it and reuses it for every later ask of the step (the wave opening's and the walk's); the owner's finally removes each one through drop_checkout/remove_base_tree, KeyboardInterrupt included; an ask made outside a step owns its own (ask_member_pins wraps itself when no owner is set). E1: names_a_pin - a member needs the checkout only when one of its resolved skills is pinned by name (_skill_places.unused_pins) or resolves in the project's copy to a pinned directory (covering_pins); none for skillPins {} or no pins. Rule B: scratch_holder(ctx, prefix) is the one placement for the checkout and the base measurement's tree: it refuses (making nothing) a temp directory under any ancestor whose .git shares the project's common git dir (read off the .git file/commondir, no git process) or within the repository top; _base_in's own check is gone. Low 7b: _loaded_tier/_stop_sentence - a project skill whose directory resolves outside the copy keeps the reader's remedy and names its real place. Windows finding (scope added): commit_label(text, checkout, sha, where, sep) is the one builder of the commit form, spelling the path under the commit with '/' on every OS and keeping a blank in the project directory; pin_stop_words is its only caller (grep of '"commit %s' in the driver: one other hit, a decision message unrelated to paths). TESTS (tests/test_drive_phase.py). Rule C: every stop scenario is judged by _observed snapshots (kind, mode, sha256) of the project tree, the trees root (executor.worktreeRoot), the lock and git's HEAD, packed-refs, index, refs, worktrees and audit-locks - before the step and at each PinStop construction (the constructor is hooked in _recorded, put back after); _stop_changes compares them minus _STOP_OWN_RECORD (lock: the state's lock key, a state file holding only the lock where none was and the directories made for it, audit-locks; scratch: the step's own registration). The audit hook stays as an aid naming the call behind a difference and the processes; _early_writes, _path_state and the old record are gone. Rule D: the driver's derivation is rewritten as an over-approximating resolver (_stop_* functions): calls resolve through names, from-imports, local imports, module aliases, parameters (values callers and defaults pass), plain local assignments, returns, IfExp/BoolOp branches, lambdas, and methods by name over top-level functions and class methods; anything else - and any raise not of a name resolving to a class - is a may-stop key unless the target is a builtin (not eval/exec) or a function of a module in _NOT_STOPPING_MODULES (named stdlib modules only). _UNRESOLVED_EXEMPT holds three rows (_fact's held, _at_point's turn, main opened by _output.terse_cli), checked both ways by spd38; _PIN_BLIND_LISTED and _pin_blind_spots are deleted; open_dispatch and step_checkout joined _STOP_ROUTES_EXEMPT, checkout_at's via is step_checkout; names_a_pin joined spd1's exemption table. Measurement (S/sg2.19/derive_measure.py over this driver, 633 top-level functions): HEAD's derivation marks 33 top routes, this one 35 with the table (2 newly marked, open_dispatch among them - a real may-stop, exempt with the old blind-list reason) and 65 without it (32 newly marked, all reached from the three table keys). Without by-name method resolution (literal reading) it marked 562 - recorded as a judgement for the orchestrator, not adopted. Windows finding (scope added): the process recorder read a Windows Popen event as one joined string (CPython's windows _execute_child runs list2cmdline before sys.audit, read in Lib/subprocess.py), so spd31 saw no git; _popen_argv splits it back (_split_cmdline), _is_git matches git/git.exe/a full path, and spd31 now says NO PROCESS RECORDED on an empty record. Low 6: spd24b's stop half compares the held re-dispatch count and asked ids before and after the stopped step. Docs: SECURITY.md, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md and CHANGELOG.md pinned-skill passages state rule A (one checkout per step, the placement), rule C (snapshot judge, aid only), rule D (the rule, not a shape list), low 5 (checkout runs the repository's hooks and filters, why faithful), low 8 (tree_unsettled None keeps and says the tree), the windows add cost 123-139 ms (2026-11-20) with the removal figure owed. Counts: spn-block 44 cases at HEAD, 53 now (tests/test_drive_phase.py --selftest --stage spn-block, ALL PASS); over HEAD's code with the new test file 44/53, the 9 red: spd1, spd22, spd23, spd24 (bookkeeping rows naming new functions), spd33a, spd34, spd34a, spd35, spd39. Mutations (S/sg2.19/mutations.py, 23 rows + 5 re-anchored + 4 windows rows): all answered as owed, private TMPDIR per run, caches purged, anchors asserted applied.
outcome.descriptive: A pin step makes one placed checkout per commit, a stop is judged by the whole state when it is raised, the stop-route derivation counts what it cannot resolve as a stop, and the two Windows CI failures are fixed at their cause.
